from_notes: If the colour of (Food + Dilute Iodine solution) changes to blue black then it indicates that [starch is present]
x: Iodine solution turns starch blue-black, so the iodine test detects starch. Sugars, fats and salt give no such colour (fat is tested with paper, sugar with Benedict's reagent).

from_notes: Hing / Asafoetida Root/rhizome Spice/condiment
x: Asafoetida is hing, the dried gum-resin from the roots of Ferula. Methi is fenugreek, saunf fennel and ajwain carom seed.

from_notes: Polysaccharides are long chains of monosaccharides linked by glycosidic bonds
x: Starch is a polysaccharide, a long chain of glucose units. Mono-, di- and oligosaccharides are single sugars or short chains.

Merthiolate (thiomersal), a mercury compound, is the classic preservative for serum and vaccines. Heparin and oxalates are anticoagulants that stop blood clotting, and formaldehyde is a tissue fixative, not a serum preservative.
source: general knowledge, not checked; printed key, not verified

from_notes: SO₂ Acid rain, respiratory diseases, damages vegetation & buildings
x: SO2 from burning coal and oil forms sulphuric acid, the main acid of acid rain; NOx adds nitric acid. Hydrochloric, formic and acetic acids are minor or absent.

from_notes: Fortification: iodised salt
x: Iodised salt is the main everyday dietary source of iodine and the chief way India prevents goitre. Seaweed is the richest natural source, but it is not a staple of our diet.
source: app notes 5:1 (runs/b5-r001/old-notes.txt) SUB 1; NextGen Rocket Biology (src/science-tech/rocket-biology.txt) p.12 (seaweed richest natural source)

x: An invar tape (nickel-steel alloy that hardly expands with heat) gives the most accurate linear measurements in surveying, for example base lines. Chains and cloth tapes are less precise.

from_notes: Examples of plant hormones include auxins, gibberellins, cytokinins, and abscisic acid.
x: Cytokinin is a plant hormone that promotes cell division. Thyroxine, oestrogen and testosterone are animal hormones.
source: OnlyIAS NCERT S&T Part 11 (src/science-tech/onlyias-ncert-science-tech-11.txt); PMF General Science Part 4 (src/science-tech/pmf-general-science-04.txt) p.1

x: MRI (MR angiography) shows the brain's blood vessels without ionising radiation and detects aneurysms. CT angiography also detects them and is often the first test, so CT is the tempting option; ECG records heart rhythm and plain X-ray does not show vessels.
evidence: https://www.barnesjewish.org/Medical-Services/Neurology-Neurosurgery/Brain-Aneurysm/Brain-Aneurysm-Diagnosis: CT/CTA, MRI/MRA and cerebral angiogram all used; angiogram most sensitive
dispute: Printed key: MRI. Strictly, CT angiography detects aneurysms as well and is often the first test; a catheter angiogram is the most sensitive (Barnes-Jewish Hospital, Brain Aneurysm Diagnosis).

from_notes: Rhodamine B | Textile dye illegally used to colour cotton candy; carcinogenic; sale banned in Tamil Nadu
x: Rhodamine B, a textile dye, was found colouring cotton candy; it is carcinogenic, so Tamil Nadu banned the sale (Feb 2024). Aristolochic acid comes from some herbal medicines, benzidine is a dye intermediate and 1,3-butadiene a rubber monomer.

In the cumene process, cumene (isopropylbenzene) is oxidised by air to cumene hydroperoxide, which dilute acid splits into phenol and acetone. Hydrogenation, benzene oxidation and propane cracking do not give phenol this way.
source: src/current-affairs/octlatest-daily-em-ca-2026-10-20.txt p.4 (phenol and acetone via the cumene process); hydroperoxide step: general knowledge, not checked

from_notes: Ethyne Calcium carbide Welding, chemical feedstock
x: Acetylene (ethyne) is used in oxy-acetylene welding and as a feedstock for plastics such as PVC. It is made from calcium carbide and water, not silicon carbide, so III is wrong.

from_notes: BPA | Polycarbonate plastics, food-can linings, thermal receipts
x: Bisphenol A is an industrial chemical used to make polycarbonate plastics and epoxy food-can linings, i.e. food-packaging materials. It is not a medical test, a doping test or an alloy steel.
source: app notes 5:1 (runs/b5-r001/old-notes.txt) SUB 0; src/environment/pmf-environment-04.txt p.101 (polycarbonate leaches bisphenol A)

from_notes: Epidemic dropsy Argemone mexicana oil → sanguinarine + dihydrosanguinarine
x: Argemone (Mexican prickly poppy) seeds look like mustard seeds and are mixed with them; their oil causes epidemic dropsy. Papaya, cumin and coriander seeds are not the usual adulterants of mustard.
source: NextGen Rocket Biology (src/science-tech/rocket-biology.txt) p.33; app notes 5:1 (runs/b5-r001/old-notes.txt) SUB 0

x: Sea water is far saltier than body fluids, so drinking it pulls more water out of the cells and worsens dehydration. Tea, coffee and alcohol are diuretics, but they still add water; sea water is the one that must not be drunk.
source: general knowledge, not checked; printed key, not verified

from_notes: BPA | Polycarbonate plastics, food-can linings, thermal receipts
x: BPA is used in polycarbonate plastics and food-can linings, so it is a chemical used for food-packaging materials. The other options (medical test, doping test, alloy steel) do not describe it.

Adding a solute lowers the water potential of a solution; it does not raise it, so (b) is the untrue statement. A solute does raise the boiling point and lower the vapour pressure, and water can be separated from a solution by distillation.

add_option: Mixture of hydrochloric acid and nitric acid (aqua regia)
from_notes: Aqua regia (3 HCl + 1 HNO₃) King of acids (dissolves gold)
x: Gold dissolves only in aqua regia, a 3:1 mixture of concentrated hydrochloric and nitric acids. No single acid dissolves it, and a sulphuric–nitric mixture does not either, so the printed key (c) is wrong.
source: NextGen Rocket Chemistry (src/science-tech/rocket-chemistry.txt) p.2, p.5, p.73; OnlyIAS NCERT S&T Part 8 (src/science-tech/onlyias-ncert-science-tech-08.txt)
evidence: NextGen Rocket Chemistry (src/science-tech/rocket-chemistry.txt) p.5: Aqua regia, mixture of HCl + HNO3 (3:1), dissolves gold
OnlyIAS NCERT S&T Part 8 (src/science-tech/onlyias-ncert-science-tech-08.txt): aqua regia = freshly prepared mixture of concentrated hydrochloric acid and nitric acid, dissolves gold

from_notes: Turmeric Rhizome (modified stem) Spice/curcumin
x: Turmeric powder is made from the dried rhizome, an underground stem, not a fruit, root or seed, so 'None of the above' is right. 'Dried root' tempts because the rhizome grows underground.
source: NextGen Rocket Biology (src/science-tech/rocket-biology.txt) p.75; PMF General Science Part 3 (src/science-tech/pmf-general-science-03.txt) p.31

x: Mustard gas (sulphur mustard) is a blistering chemical-warfare agent. It has nothing to do with mustard oil, fuels or deodorants.
source: general knowledge, not checked; src/environment/shankar-environment-06.ocr.txt p.8 (mustard gas listed with asbestos, arsenic as hazards)

from_notes: Mustard oil is NOT a lubricant: mineral oil = petroleum; vegetable fats = phytosterol; animal fats = cholesterol.
x: Mustard oil is an edible vegetable oil, not a lubricant, so that pair is wrong. Mineral oil comes from petroleum, vegetable fats contain phytosterols and animal fats contain cholesterol.

from_notes: Ethyne Calcium carbide + water
x: Calcium carbide reacts with moisture to give acetylene, which acts like the ripening hormone ethylene, so it is (illegally) used to ripen mangoes. Calcium sulphide, carbonate and chloride release no such gas.
source: NextGen Rocket Chemistry (src/science-tech/rocket-chemistry.txt) p.27; PMF General Science Part 7 (src/science-tech/pmf-general-science-07.txt) p.60 (ethylene ripens fruit)

x: Mustard gas (sulphur mustard) was used as a chemical weapon in World War I, along with chlorine and phosgene. Carbon monoxide and hydrogen cyanide were not the typical battlefield agents.
Prussic acid is hydrocyanic acid (HCN), whose salts are the cyanides. Sulphuric, hydrochloric and nitric acids are mineral acids, not cyanide.
source: general knowledge, not checked; PMF General Science Part 7 (src/science-tech/pmf-general-science-07.txt) p.2 (cyanide is highly toxic)

from_notes: Aflatoxin toxicity Aspergillus flavus / A. parasiticus → aflatoxin
x: Aflatoxins are made by moulds (Aspergillus flavus and A. parasiticus) that grow on badly stored grain and oilseeds. Bacteria, protozoa and viruses do not produce them.

from_notes: Aflatoxin toxicity Aspergillus flavus / A. parasiticus → aflatoxin
x: Aflatoxins are poisonous, cancer-causing chemicals made by moulds such as Aspergillus flavus on stored grain; cooking does not destroy them. Bacteria, protozoa and viruses are wrong.

from_notes: Ethyne Calcium carbide + water
x: Calcium carbide gives acetylene, which ripens fruit like ethylene, so it is the chemical used for (artificial) ripening. Sodium and potassium chloride have no ripening action.

from_notes: Sorbic acid / potassium sorbate Cheese, cooked foods, pickles (yeasts & moulds)
x: Sorbic acid and its salt potassium sorbate are the commonest preservatives against moulds, yeasts and fungi. Tartaric acid is a food acid, acetylsalicylic acid is aspirin and formic acid only a limited preservative.

from_notes: Formic acid HCOOH Ant stings, bee stings, nettle
x: Nettle leaf hairs inject formic (methanoic) acid, causing the burning pain. Acetic acid is vinegar, phosphoric acid is in colas and sulphuric acid is a mineral acid.
source: NextGen Rocket Chemistry (src/science-tech/rocket-chemistry.txt) p.19; OnlyIAS NCERT S&T Part 7 (src/science-tech/onlyias-ncert-science-tech-07.txt)

from_notes: Highest percentage of carbohydrate Rice
x: Rice is mostly starch, so carbohydrate is its major nutrient. Its protein is only about 7%, and vitamins and minerals are minor.

from_notes: Fructose: It is the sweetest naturally occurring sugar.
x: Fructose is the sweetest natural sugar, followed by sucrose, glucose and maltose. The other orders put glucose, maltose or sucrose first.
source: PMF General Science Part 2 (src/science-tech/pmf-general-science-02.txt) p.55 (fructose sweetest); full order: general knowledge, not checked

x: In the breath analyser, orange acidified potassium dichromate turns green as it oxidises the alcohol in the breath. Permanganate, silica gel and baking soda are not used.

from_notes: Fructose (fruit sugar): It is the sweetest naturally occurring sugar. It is found in fruits and honey.
x: Honey is mainly fructose (about 38%), with slightly less glucose; sucrose and maltose are minor. So fructose is its largest component.

from_notes: [ethanol reacts with sodium to give] sodium ethoxide. This reaction supports the acidic character of ethanol.
x: Ethanol reacts with sodium to give sodium ethoxide and hydrogen gas. Sodium acetate, ethanoic acid and ethyl acetate need oxidation or esterification instead.

from_notes: Saccharin Artificial sweetener; Alitame ~2000x sucrose - highest
x: Saccharin was the first popular artificial sweetener, aspartame is (in NCERT's words) about 100 times as sweet as cane sugar, and alitame is a high-potency sweetener. So I-c, II-a, III-b.
source: NextGen Rocket Chemistry (src/science-tech/rocket-chemistry.txt) p.51 (alitame highest potency); NCERT Class XII Chemistry 'Chemistry in Everyday Life' wording: general knowledge, not checked

from_notes: Fatty acid Source / significance
x: Lipids (fats) are made of fatty acids joined to glycerol. Glucose and fructose build carbohydrates, and amino acids build proteins.

from_notes: Formic acid HCOOH Ant stings, bee stings, nettle
x: School books and Rocket list formic (methanoic) acid as the acid of a bee sting. Lactic, malic and citric acids come from muscles, apples and lemons.

Sodium hypochlorite (bleach) is an oxidising agent that breaks down the coloured compounds of tea and coffee stains on white cloth. Water and lemon juice only lighten fresh stains, and petrol removes grease, not coffee.
source: general knowledge, not checked; byjus.com question-answer page (search result, not opened) gives sodium hypochlorite
evidence: web search: BYJU'S Q&A 'coffee stains ... can be properly removed by' keys sodium hypochlorite (page returned 404 when opened)

from_notes: Fructose (fruit sugar): ... found in fruits and honey.
x: Honey is mainly fructose (about 38%) with slightly less glucose, so fructose is its major sugar. Sucrose and maltose are only minor components.

from_notes: Phosphoric acid H₃PO₄ Soft drinks, fertilizers
x: Cola drinks are acidified with phosphoric acid, which gives their tangy taste. Formic, lactic and acetic acids are not cola ingredients.

from_notes: Sodium benzoate (C₇H₅NaO₂) Soft drinks, acidic foods, fruit juice (E211)
x: Sodium benzoate (E211) is a food preservative that stops bacteria, yeast and moulds in acidic foods and drinks. It is not a flavour, colour or antacid.

Formic acid is stronger than acetic acid because acetic acid's CH3 group pushes electrons and weakens it. Formic acid is also an organic acid, but that does not explain why it is stronger, so both are true and R is not the explanation.
source: general knowledge, not checked (pKa formic 3.75, acetic 4.76)

from_notes: Ant bites inject the acidic liquid (formic acid)
x: Ants inject formic acid (from Latin formica, ant), which causes the burning sensation. Acetic acid, methanol and stearic acid are not involved.
source: OnlyIAS NCERT S&T Part 7 (src/science-tech/onlyias-ncert-science-tech-07.txt); NextGen Rocket Chemistry (src/science-tech/rocket-chemistry.txt) p.19

from_notes: Chlorine Cl Used in water purification
x: Chlorine reacts with water to form hypochlorous acid (HOCl) and HCl; HOCl is the strong disinfectant that kills microbes. HCl does not disinfect, and 'nascent oxygen' is an older textbook explanation.
source: NextGen Rocket Chemistry (src/science-tech/rocket-chemistry.txt) p.4 (chlorine in water purification); HOCl mechanism: general knowledge, not checked

from_notes: Nylon W.H. Carothers (DuPont) 1935 First fully synthetic fiber
x: Nylon was the first fully synthetic fibre (Carothers, 1935). Wool, silk and leather are natural protein polymers.

from_notes: Most reactive metal Potassium (K) Reactivity series top
x: Potassium is at the top of the reactivity series (K > Na > Ca > Fe), so it is the most reactive of the four metals.

from_notes: Kitchen: colas contain phosphoric acid and caffeine
x: Colas contain significant caffeine, a stimulant alkaloid. Nicotine is in tobacco, tannin in tea and renin is a kidney enzyme.

from_notes: cobalt, and selenium are needed by higher plants [list of essential elements]
x: Boron, zinc and copper are essential plant micronutrients; sodium is not required by most plants. So sodium is the answer.

from_notes: Citric acid C₆H₈O₇ Citrus fruits (lemon, orange, lime)
x: Lemon contains citric acid. Acetic acid is in vinegar, ascorbic acid is vitamin C and nitric acid is a mineral acid.
source: NextGen Rocket Chemistry (src/science-tech/rocket-chemistry.txt) p.19; NextGen Rocket Biology (src/science-tech/rocket-biology.txt) p.12

from_notes: Fructose (fruit sugar): It is the sweetest naturally occurring sugar. It is found in fruits and honey.
x: Fructose (fruit sugar) gives fruits their sweet taste. Maltose is malt sugar, lactose milk sugar and ribose a sugar of RNA.

from_notes: Potato Black heart/Krishnakant Oxygen deficiency
x: Blackheart of potato is a storage disorder caused by oxygen deficiency in the tuber's centre. It is not caused by a copper, boron or potassium deficiency.

from_notes: Ant bites inject the acidic liquid (formic acid)
x: Ants inject formic acid, a simple carboxylic acid. Glacial acetic acid, methanol and stearic acid are wrong.
source: OnlyIAS NCERT S&T Part 7 (src/science-tech/onlyias-ncert-science-tech-07.txt); NextGen Rocket Chemistry (src/science-tech/rocket-chemistry.txt) p.19

from_notes: Invert sugar (glucose + fructose) Sweeter than sucrose
x: Invert sugar (glucose + fructose) is sweeter than sucrose because of its free fructose. It is made by hydrolysing sucrose, which is true but is not why it is sweeter.

from_notes: Acetic acid CH₃COOH Vinegar
x: Vinegar is dilute acetic acid, whose IUPAC name is ethanoic acid. Formic acid is the ant-sting acid and malic acid is in apples.

from_notes: Fructose (fruit sugar): ... found in fruits and honey.
x: Fructose predominates in honey, slightly ahead of glucose. Sucrose, galactose and maltose are minor or absent.

from_notes: Gel Liquid Solid Jelly, Butter, Cheese
x: Cheese is a gel, a colloid of a liquid dispersed in a solid. Milk is an emulsion (liquid in liquid), mud a suspension and rubber a polymer.

from_notes: Reactivity Series (high to low): K > Na > Ca > Mg > Al > Zn > Fe > Pb
x: Zinc is more reactive than tin, so it would react with food acids and form harmful salts; tin is less reactive and safe. Cost and melting point are not the reason.

from_notes: Benzoic acid Food preservative (as salts)
x: Benzoic acid (as sodium benzoate) is a standard food-processing preservative. Sodium carbonate, acetylene and sodium nitrate are not the usual answer.

from_notes: Highest concentration of citrate among citrus fruits Lemon
x: Lemon contains citric acid in free form. Tamarind mainly has tartaric acid, apple malic acid and milk lactic acid.
source: NextGen Rocket Biology (src/science-tech/rocket-biology.txt) p.12; NextGen Rocket Chemistry (src/science-tech/rocket-chemistry.txt) p.19

from_notes: Sucralose A non-caloric sweetener made from sugar but modified
x: Sucralose is made by replacing hydroxyl groups of sucrose with chlorine, so it is a modified sugar. Aspartame is a dipeptide, saccharin and alitame are not made from sugar.
Chicory powder is made from the roasted, ground root of the chicory plant, so the answer is root.

from_notes: Rancidity: When fats and oils are oxidised, they become rancid and their smell and taste [change]
x: Fats and oils turn rancid when they are oxidised by air, which is why the manufacture date of fried food matters. Reduction and hydrogenation do not cause rancidity.

from_notes: Carbonic acid H₂CO₃ Soda water, rain water (with CO₂)
x: CO2 dissolves in water to form carbonic acid, so soda water is acidic. It is not basic, and it is neither an oxidising nor a reducing agent.
source: NextGen Rocket Chemistry (src/science-tech/rocket-chemistry.txt) p.19; PMF General Science Part 7 (src/science-tech/pmf-general-science-07.txt) p.27

from_notes: Reduced oxygen Slows respiration & ripening of fruits/vegetables
x: Low temperature slows the respiration rate of fruits, so they ripen and decay more slowly and keep longer. Darkness, CO2 or humidity are not the main reason.
source: NextGen Rocket Chemistry (src/science-tech/rocket-chemistry.txt) p.51 (slower respiration extends storage); cold effect: general knowledge, not checked

from_notes: Grains: Whole grains (e.g., brown rice, whole wheat bread, oatmeal)
x: Oatmeal is made from oats, a cereal grain. Sago and arrowroot are starches from palm stems and roots, and soya flour comes from a legume.
IQF stands for Individually Quick Frozen, a technique where each piece of food is frozen separately and rapidly to keep texture and quality.

from_notes: Ethylene (C₂H₄) ... plant hormones for ripening fruits
x: Ethylene is the gaseous plant hormone that promotes fruit ripening. Cytokinin promotes cell division and abscisic acid is a growth inhibitor.
source: PMF General Science Part 7 (src/science-tech/pmf-general-science-07.txt) p.58, p.60

from_notes: [baking powder contains baking soda and] a mild edible acid such as tartaric acid
x: Baking powder is baking soda plus a mild edible acid, tartaric acid. Oxalic acid is toxic, and lactic and benzoic acids are not its acid component.
Animal (bone) charcoal is used to decolourise raw sugar in refining because it adsorbs the coloured impurities. Wood, sugar and coconut charcoal are not the standard answer.
source: general knowledge, not checked; printed key, not verified

x: Poaching cooks food gently in a small amount of hot liquid at about 160–180 °F, as for eggs. Blanching is a brief dip in boiling water, baking uses dry oven heat and broiling direct heat.
Chicory powder used as a coffee additive is made from the roasted roots of the chicory plant, not its stem, leaves or seeds.

from_notes: Ethylene (C₂H₄) ... plant hormones for ripening fruits
x: Ethylene is the gas (plant hormone) used for artificial ripening of green fruit. Acetylene from calcium carbide only imitates it, and ethane and CO2 do not ripen fruit.

from_notes: Emulsion Liquid Liquid Milk, Cream, Mayonnaise
x: Milk is an emulsion, fat droplets dispersed in water (oil-in-water). A gel is liquid in solid, a foam gas in liquid, and milk is not a suspension.

from_notes: Pepsin breaks [proteins into peptides]
x: Pepsin, from the chief cells of the stomach, breaks proteins into small peptides. Trypsin and peptidases act in the small intestine and lipase digests fats.
source: PMF General Science Part 2 (src/science-tech/pmf-general-science-02.txt) p.42; OnlyIAS NCERT S&T Part 10 (src/science-tech/onlyias-ncert-science-tech-10.txt)

from_notes: C Ascorbic acid Collagen, wound healing, iron absorption, antioxidant Scurvy / bleeding gums
x: Ascorbic acid is vitamin C, and its deficiency causes scurvy. Kwashiorkor is protein deficiency, glossitis is B2 and beri-beri B1.
Scorpion venom toxins are small proteins (peptides) that act on nerve ion channels. They are not vitamins, cyanides or alkalis.

from_notes: Kwashiorkor is caused by protein deficiency without calorie shortage
x: Kwashiorkor results from protein deficiency in a diet that may have enough calories. Vitamin, carbohydrate or water deficiency do not cause it.

from_notes: golden rice (Vitamin 'A' enriched rice)
x: Golden rice carries genes for beta-carotene, the precursor of vitamin A. It is not designed for vitamin B, C or omega-3.
source: OnlyIAS NCERT S&T Part 12 (src/science-tech/onlyias-ncert-science-tech-12.txt); src/science-tech/pmf-science-tech-03.txt p.24

from_notes: B2 Riboflavin; B3 Niacin; B6 Pyridoxine; B7 Biotin / Vitamin-H
x: B2 is riboflavin, B6 pyridoxine, B3 niacin and B7 biotin, so I-b, II-d, III-a, IV-c.

from_notes: Marasmus is caused by a lack of both proteins and calories, usually in infants
x: Marasmus results from severe lack of both protein and calories. Scurvy is vitamin C deficiency, goitre iodine deficiency and mumps a viral disease.
Vitamin C is the vitamin most easily destroyed by heat (and by oxidation). The B group is partly heat-stable, and A and E are fat-soluble and more stable in cooking.

from_notes: Umetaro Suzuki Extracted water-soluble micronutrient mixture from rice bran
x: Thiamine (B1) is in the bran and husk layer of rice, which is why polished rice causes beri-beri. Carrot and beetroot are not B1 sources, and sunflower seeds are not the answer here.
source: NextGen Rocket Biology (src/science-tech/rocket-biology.txt) p.42; app notes 5:1 (runs/b5-r001/old-notes.txt) SUB 2 (polished rice → beri-beri)

from_notes: Thalassemia is an inherited blood disorder where the body produces fewer healthy haemoglobin
x: Thalassemia is an autosomal recessive disorder with a reduced rate of synthesis of one of the globin chains (α or β) of haemoglobin. X-linked inheritance is haemophilia, a clotting-protein defect is also haemophilia, and phenylalanine build-up is PKU.
evidence: PMF General Science Part 4 (src/science-tech/pmf-general-science-04.txt) p.20 (haemophilia = X-linked, clotting)
PMF General Science Part 4 (src/science-tech/pmf-general-science-04.txt) p.23 (PKU: phenylalanine build-up)

from_notes: α-Keratin → horn, nail, hoof, hair, skin
x: Keratin (hair, nails) and myosin (muscle) are both proteins. Fructose, maltose and sucrose are sugars, so the other pairs are not only proteins.

from_notes: B2 Riboflavin Metabolism Cheilosis, glossitis, dermatosis, digestive disorders
x: Riboflavin (B2) deficiency causes cheilosis and digestive disorders. Pernicious anaemia is B12, vitamin E is not about clotting, and vitamin K deficiency prolongs clotting time.
Lactoderm is the name of the sticky protein skin that forms on top of heated milk. The other options are made-up words.
source: general knowledge, not checked; printed key, not verified

x: In ruminants, the abomasum is the true glandular stomach that secretes pepsin and HCl. The rumen, reticulum and omasum produce no gastric juice.
source: general knowledge, not checked; src/environment/pmf-environment-02.txt p.25 (four-chambered ruminant stomach ending in abomasum)

x: The Kjeldahl method measures nitrogen, which is multiplied by 6.25 to give crude protein. Crude fibre, ether extract (fat) and ash have their own methods.
Cage layer fatigue is a bone disorder of laying hens prevented by enough vitamin D, calcium and phosphorus in feed, so 'all of these' is right.
source: general knowledge, not checked; printed key, not verified

from_notes: The 9 essential amino acids are histidine, isoleucine, leucine, lysine, methionine, phenylalanine, threonine, tryptophan, and valine.
x: Isoleucine is one of the essential amino acids that must come from food. Alanine, aspartic acid and cysteine are made in the body.

from_notes: Vitamin A Night blindness; Vitamin C Scurvy; Vitamin D Rickets; Vitamin K Bleeding tendency
x: Vitamin A – night blindness, D – rickets, C – scurvy, K – excessive bleeding, so A-2, B-4, C-1, D-3.

from_notes: Vitamin A Night blindness; Vitamin D Rickets; Iodine Goitre
x: Malaria spreads by mosquito bite, goitre is iodine deficiency, rickets vitamin D deficiency and night blindness vitamin A deficiency, so 1-d, 2-c, 3-a, 4-b.
source: NextGen Rocket Biology (src/science-tech/rocket-biology.txt) p.33 (malaria, Anopheles), p.43

from_notes: Kwashiorkor is caused by protein deficiency without calorie shortage
x: Kwashiorkor is caused by protein deficiency. Water deficiency, pollution and viruses do not cause it.

from_notes: The 9 essential amino acids are histidine, isoleucine, leucine, lysine, methionine, phenylalanine, threonine, tryptophan, and valine.
x: Tyrosine is non-essential because the body makes it from phenylalanine. Methionine, tryptophan and threonine are essential.
source: PMF General Science Part 3 (src/science-tech/pmf-general-science-03.txt) p.2; PMF General Science Part 4 (src/science-tech/pmf-general-science-04.txt) p.23 (phenylalanine → tyrosine)

from_notes: B7 Biotin / Vitamin-H
x: Biotin is vitamin B7, not B12 (B12 is cobalamin), so that pair is incorrect. Thiamin B1, riboflavin B2 and niacin B3 are correct.

from_notes: C Ascorbic acid
x: Vitamin C is ascorbic acid. Hydrochloric, sulphuric and acetic acids are not vitamins.
source: NextGen Rocket Biology (src/science-tech/rocket-biology.txt) p.41; NextGen Rocket Chemistry (src/science-tech/rocket-chemistry.txt) p.19

from_notes: B12 Cobalamin / Cyanocobalamin
x: Vitamin B12 is cobalamin. Riboflavin is B2, pyridoxine B6 and pantothenic acid B5.
Zein, a prolamin, is the principal protein of maize, as gluten is of wheat.
Papaya, mango, peaches and apricots are rich in antioxidants (beta-carotene, vitamin C), carbohydrates and soluble fibre; they are poor in protein and fat. So a, c and d.

from_notes: Vitamin B12 Pernicious anaemia
x: Vitamin B12 (cobalamin) is the anti-pernicious-anaemia factor; its deficiency causes pernicious anaemia.

from_notes: Amino acids Building blocks of proteins
x: Proteins are synthesised from amino acids, their building blocks.

from_notes: C Ascorbic acid ... Scurvy / bleeding gums
x: Scurvy is caused by deficiency of ascorbic acid (vitamin C).

from_notes: Vitamin C Amla
x: Amla (Indian gooseberry) is the richest common source of vitamin C; chilli is the richest among vegetables.
Double toned milk has 1.5% fat (and 9% SNF); toned milk has 3% fat.

from_notes: Protein source with all essential amino acids Egg
x: Egg proteins have high biological value because they contain all the essential amino acids in the right proportion.

from_notes: Vitamin C Scurvy
x: Vitamin C deficiency causes scurvy (bleeding gums, poor wound healing).

from_notes: Casein → major milk protein
x: Caseins are the primary group of milk proteins (about 80% of cow's milk protein); whey proteins make up the rest. Lactoferrin and albumin are minor.
source: NextGen Rocket Biology (src/science-tech/rocket-biology.txt) p.45; PMF General Science Part 3 (src/science-tech/pmf-general-science-03.txt) p.4

from_notes: Cobalt Component of B12
x: Vitamin B12 (cobalamin) contains cobalt. B1, B2 and B6 have no metal.

from_notes: Protein Growth + repair + body tissue building
x: Muscle is built from protein, so athletes need a high-protein diet. Calories, vitamins and glucose give energy or regulation, not muscle tissue.

from_notes: [thyroid makes] thyroxine (T4) and triiodothyronine (T3)
x: Thyroxine (T4) contains iodine, which is why iodine deficiency causes goitre. Insulin, testosterone and adrenaline contain no iodine.
source: PMF General Science Part 3 (src/science-tech/pmf-general-science-03.txt) p.52; NextGen Rocket Biology (src/science-tech/rocket-biology.txt) p.43

x: None of these is a natural vitamin D source (fresh fruits and seeds have almost none); only orange juice, which is often fortified, supplies some, so orange is the best of the four.
source: https://www.webmd.com/diet/foods-high-in-vitamin-d (fortified orange juice 2.5 mcg per cup; seeds and berries not listed)
evidence: https://www.webmd.com/diet/foods-high-in-vitamin-d: fortified orange juice listed; seeds and strawberries not listed
web search: USDA-based tables give 0 µg vitamin D for pumpkin and sunflower seeds and strawberries
dispute: Printed key: none. Strictly, none of the four contains vitamin D naturally; orange counts only as fortified orange juice (WebMD, Foods High in Vitamin D).

from_notes: B2 Riboflavin
x: Vitamin B2 is riboflavin. Pyridoxine is B6, thiamine B1 and cyanocobalamin B12.
Cod-liver oil has by far the most vitamin A (retinol) per gram – many times more than carrots or pumpkin (beta-carotene) or egg.

from_notes: Carbohydrate Immediate/main energy source
x: Carbohydrates are the primary energy-giving food. Proteins build the body, and vitamins and minerals regulate it.
Rafting ties several logs together into a raft that floats downstream as one unit. Floating moves logs loose, one by one, and rope-ways and tramways are overland methods.

from_notes: Dialysis Artificial filtration
x: Dialysis filters wastes and excess water from blood, but cannot reabsorb useful nutrients as the kidney tubules do. Waste removal, water balance and stopping toxic build-up are things it does.
source: NextGen Rocket Biology (src/science-tech/rocket-biology.txt) p.56; PMF General Science Part 2 (src/science-tech/pmf-general-science-02.txt) p.52

from_notes: A Retinol ... Night blindness, xerophthalmia
x: Vitamin A deficiency causes night blindness and xerophthalmia, leading to vision loss and blindness. Rickets is vitamin D, and clotting problems are vitamin K.

from_notes: Protein Growth + repair + body tissue building
x: Proteins are the body-building nutrients. Carbohydrates and fats give energy and vitamins regulate.

from_notes: Haemophilia is a sex-linked recessive disorder that affects blood clotting.
x: Haemophilia is an inherited (X-linked) disorder in which blood does not clot. Anaemia and thalassemia lower haemoglobin, and blood cancer is leukaemia.

from_notes: Gluten → wheat; bread-making quality
x: Gluten is the protein of wheat that gives dough its elasticity.

from_notes: Vitamin C Amla
x: Gooseberry (amla) is the richest common source of vitamin C.

from_notes: B3 Niacin Metabolism Pellagra
x: Niacin (B3) deficiency causes pellagra. Scurvy is C, rickets D and beri-beri B1.
Rickets in chickens is caused by vitamin D3 deficiency; birds use D3 (cholecalciferol) far better than D2. Vitamins A, B12 and E cause other disorders.
High blood pressure, high blood glucose and raised lipids are risk factors for heart disease; vitamin A deficiency is not, so it is the answer.
source: general knowledge, not checked; NextGen Rocket Biology (src/science-tech/rocket-biology.txt) p.45 (saturated fat, trans fat raise lipids and CVD risk)

from_notes: C Ascorbic acid Collagen, wound healing, iron absorption, antioxidant
x: Vitamin C is needed for collagen, so its deficiency gives dry damaged skin, slow wound healing and easy bruising (scurvy). Vitamins D, A and B12 cause bone, eye and anaemia problems.

from_notes: D Calciferol ... Rickets, osteomalacia
x: Osteomalacia, softening of adult bones, is caused by vitamin D deficiency. Carbohydrate, iodine and vitamin C are wrong.
source: NextGen Rocket Biology (src/science-tech/rocket-biology.txt) p.41; PMF General Science Part 3 (src/science-tech/pmf-general-science-03.txt) p.14

from_notes: Marasmus is caused by a lack of both proteins and calories
x: Marasmic kwashiorkor results from deficiency of both proteins and calories (wasting with oedema). Goitre is iodine, achondroplasia genetic and rickets vitamin D.

at: a, c, b, e and d
x: Protein per 100 g rises from egg white (~11 g) to fish (~20 g), Bengal gram dal (~21 g), groundnut (~25 g) and skimmed milk powder (~35 g). So a, c, b, e, d.
source: general knowledge, not checked; printed key, not verified

x: Vitamin C (ascorbic acid) is a strong reducing agent, so on cut fruit exposed to air it is lost by oxidation.
source: NextGen Rocket Biology (src/science-tech/rocket-biology.txt) p.41 (vitamin C antioxidant); oxidation loss: general knowledge, not checked

from_notes: Fat-soluble: A, D, E, K [Rocket: A, D, E, K Fat]
x: Statements a (Funk coined 'vitamine'), b (vitamins are organic) and c (K for clotting) are true; d is false because A, D, E and K are fat-soluble. So only d.
A virus is nucleic acid (DNA or RNA) inside a protein coat. It has no metabolism of its own, so the defining content is nucleic acid, not enzymes, carbohydrates or vitamins.

from_notes: B1 Thiamine ... Beri-beri
x: Thiamine is vitamin B1, whose deficiency causes beri-beri.

from_notes: Amino acids Building blocks of proteins
x: Amino acids are the building blocks of proteins. Ribosomes make proteins, glucose builds carbohydrates and fatty acids build fats.

from_notes: Vitamin B9 (Folic ... Megaloblastic anaemia
x: Macrocytic (megaloblastic) anaemia results from deficiency of folic acid (folacin) or B12. Biotin, niacin and pantothenic acid do not cause it.

from_notes: Protein Growth + repair + body tissue building
x: Proteins are the body-building nutrient, essential for the growth of children. Milk is a food, not a nutrient, and fats and vitamins do not build tissue.

Cow's milk is slightly yellow because of carotene (beta-carotene) in its fat; 'Carolin' is the paper's misprint of carotin (carotene). Riboflavin only gives whey a greenish-yellow tint, so the printed key (b) is wrong.
evidence: https://www.vedantu.com/question-answer/cows-milk-is-slightly-yellowish-in-color-due-to-class-11-biology-cbse-5fbac2cfa8ffee1f309d0ae4: answer carotene; riboflavin is not the pigment
web search: carotene in milk fat gives yellow; riboflavin gives whey a greenish-yellow tone
PMF General Science Part 1 (src/science-tech/pmf-general-science-01.txt) p.42 (carotene is a fat-soluble yellow pigment)

from_notes: Highest protein content Soybean
x: Soybean has about 40% protein and 20% fat besides carbohydrate, so it is rich in all three. Rice is mainly carbohydrate, and mango and cabbage are poor in protein and fat.

from_notes: B12 Cobalamin / Cyanocobalamin
x: Cyanocobalamin is the synthetic, cobalt-containing form of vitamin B12.

from_notes: D Calciferol ... Calcium/bone metabolism
x: Vitamin D controls calcium and bone metabolism, so it is needed for bones and teeth; its deficiency causes rickets.
Vitamin D is made in the skin on exposure to sunlight, so it is called the sunshine vitamin. Vitamins A, C and K are not made this way.

from_notes: B2 Riboflavin Metabolism Cheilosis, glossitis, dermatosis, digestive disorders
x: Riboflavin (B2) deficiency causes sore throat, cheilosis, stomatitis, glossitis and dermatitis. Ascorbic acid is C (scurvy), retinol A and cyanocobalamin B12.

from_notes: Carbohydrate main energy; Fat stored energy; Protein growth + repair
x: Plants make carbohydrates, fats and proteins as essential foods for human and animal metabolism. Nucleic acids (DNA, RNA) are genetic material, not a food group.
Proline is one of the 20 amino acids that make up proteins (a non-essential one). It is not a base, a bacterium or a virus.

from_notes: Kwashiorkor (edema, stunted growth)
x: Kwashiorkor (protein deficiency) typically shows oedema (swelling). Marasmus is wasting without oedema, and hypertension and fever do not feature oedema as a typical sign.
source: PMF General Science Part 3 (src/science-tech/pmf-general-science-03.txt) p.19; PMF General Science Part 2 (src/science-tech/pmf-general-science-02.txt) p.46

from_notes: Vitamin Regulatory/metabolic functions in small amounts
x: Vitamins are micronutrients needed in small amounts, whereas protein, carbohydrates and fats are macronutrients.

from_notes: Pyridoxine = vitamin B6: amino-acid metabolism and antibody production
x: Vitamin B6 (pyridoxine) is needed for amino-acid metabolism and antibody production. B12 is for RBCs, B1 for carbohydrate metabolism and B2 for energy release.
source: app notes 5:1 (runs/b5-r001/old-notes.txt) SUB 2; NextGen Rocket Biology (src/science-tech/rocket-biology.txt) p.41

from_notes: Parboiling (soak + steam) raises rice's nutritive value: B vitamins move from bran into grain
x: Parboiling drives water-soluble B vitamins and minerals from the husk and bran into the grain, so rice's nutritive value increases.

from_notes: Vitamin K sources: green leafy vegetables, also nuts, eggs and animal liver
x: Nuts, eggs and animal liver supply vitamin K, which is the exam key. Green leafy vegetables are the best-known source, but tomatoes and carrots are poor, so option (c) is not a clean answer; shark-liver oil gives vitamins A and D.
source: app notes 5:1 (runs/b5-r001/old-notes.txt) SUB 2; PMF General Science Part 3 (src/science-tech/pmf-general-science-03.txt) p.14 (green leafy vegetables)
dispute: APPSC 2004 key: nuts, eggs, liver. Strictly, green leafy vegetables are the richest source of vitamin K (PMF General Science Part 3 p.14), but option (c) adds tomatoes and carrots, which are poor sources.

from_notes: Caffeine (tea, coffee, colas) is a diuretic; citric acid is not a substitute for ascorbic acid
from_notes_src: UPSC CSE 2006 official key; NextGen Rocket Chemistry (src/science-tech/rocket-chemistry.txt) p.19
x: Caffeine is a diuretic, citric acid is used in soft drinks and ascorbic acid (vitamin C) is needed for collagen in bones and teeth. Citric acid cannot replace ascorbic acid, so 1, 2 and 3 only.
source: NextGen Rocket Chemistry (src/science-tech/rocket-chemistry.txt) p.19; NextGen Rocket Biology (src/science-tech/rocket-biology.txt) p.41 (vitamin C: collagen)

from_notes: Richest natural source of iodine Seaweed
x: Seaweeds are the richest natural source of iodine. Chlorine and bromine are not what seaweeds are prized for.
